papers.title: Coherent synchrotron radiation extraction from a bent beam pipe
papers.abstract: Coherent synchrotron radiation generated in a bending magnet can propagate far downstream and heat the beam pipe. We investigate a beam-free side outlet that diverts part of this radiation into a separate guide. We use a paraxial equation to calculate radiation generation in the bend and its division between the two guides. Modal and finite-difference solutions are used in the bend, and quadratic finite elements on a changing transverse mesh in the branching region. We check the paraxial approximation against full-wave solutions at selected frequencies. Separately, we calculate radiation attenuation in a conducting pipe without an outlet using complex modes that satisfy impedance boundary conditions. For this example, independently damped perfectly conducting modes underestimate the high-frequency transmitted power. For a $70\times25$ mm rectangular chamber with a $30^\circ$ bend of radius 2.2 m and Gaussian bunches of rms length $10\,\mu$m, the selected outlet diverts about 53\% of the total outgoing radiation power into the beam-free channel.

papers.title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I--type-II boundary: the low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
papers.abstract: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field $B_{\rm sh}$ of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on Nb. Ginzburg--Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large-$\kappa$ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low-$\kappa$ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with $\kappa_{\rm GL}=0.7$, we obtain $B_{\rm sh}\simeq 290\,{\rm mT}$ at $T/T_c=0.2$, using $B_{c0}\simeq 200\,{\rm mT}$. For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner-stability limit of about $67\,{\rm MV/m}$.
